name: Indian Overseas Bank
title: Indian Overseas Bank - 532388 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: IOB posted FY26 net profit of about Rs 5,208 crore (up 56.16%) and advances growth of 24.16%, with GNPA down to 1.42%.
summary.overview: Indian Overseas Bank reported a strong Q4 FY26 and full-year FY26, with total business up 20.76% to Rs 6,78,614 crore and advances up 24.16% to Rs 3,10,423 crore. Net profit rose 56.16% to about Rs 5,208 crore, ROA reached 1.23% and ROE 20.42%. Asset quality improved, with GNPA at 1.42% and NNPA at 0.21%. Management guided to 14-16% industry credit growth, flagged ECL front-loading of about Rs 3,000 crore (Rs 1,750 crore already provided), and said it sees no West Asia stress so far.

financial_highlights.change: up 15.40% from Rs 8,688 crore; stated as all-time high

financial_highlights.value: Rs 2,732 crore (Rs 2,796 crore cited in Q&A)
financial_highlights.change: up 15.91% (Rs 2,357 crore prior year); 15.63% cited in Q&A

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail advances Rs 91,086 crore, 30.94% of domestic advances, up 45.12% YoY. RAM is 83% of domestic advances; management says RAM remains the priority.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agri advances Rs 1,03,821 crore, up about 40% YoY and 35.26% of domestic advances. About 70% of gold loans are agri-classified; gold loans are about 30% of total credit.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances Rs 50,107 crore, up 13.08% YoY; core MSME growth 23.77%, 17.02% of domestic advances. MSME NPA ratio cited at about 2-2.4%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate and others are 17% of domestic advances; corporate NPA about 0.24% of NPA. Rs 13,000 crore sanctioned corporate pipeline cited.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Overseas advances were flat YoY by management's account, which is deliberate. Overseas NPAs are legacy 2015-2017 accounts pending in courts, and overseas yield on advances is 8.92% versus 9.08% domestic.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Domestic investments Rs 1,15,730 crore and global investments Rs 1,19,810 crore. Yield on investments 6.66%; management sees no large treasury gains in the next two quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM in the 3.30-3.35% range going forward.
Management sees 14-16% credit growth for the industry, which it says IOB can exceed; it targets 13-15% growth in key parameters annually.
ECL: total impact expected at about Rs 3,000 crore; Rs 1,750 crore already provided. Management intends to front-load fully rather than use the five-year spread.
ECLGS 5.0 could add Rs 8,000-10,000 crore of funding; about 25-30% of the portfolio may be eligible; scheme valid to March 2027.
Recovery target for FY27 cut to about Rs 3,600 crore from more than Rs 4,000 crore previously, as NPA stock has declined.
Baseline ROA floor of above 1.20%; no formal ROE/ROA aspirational target. Management plans a QIP in FY27 to improve float.
capex_capacity: Domestic branches 3,494 (up about 160 in FY26), of which about 2,040 rural and semi-urban.
ATMs 3,651 (3,497 a year earlier); BC points 12,187.
Technology investment rising year on year, up to 15%, per management.
Mobile banking users about 35 lakh, with about 15,000 enrolments per day; registered mobile banking users 129.58 lakh; internet banking 39.5 lakh; UPI registered users 157.62 lakh.
demand_pricing: Deposit growth of 18.03% was ahead of the bank's own 12-15% targets; CASA grew 10.85%. Cost of deposits fell to 4.97%.
Yield on advances: domestic 9.08%, global 8.84% (8.92% overseas as quoted in Q&A). Yield on funds 8.10%.
Management rejects low-margin AAA corporate lending priced at about 6-6.25%, preferring higher-margin RAM lending.
Digital sourcing is about 21-22% of retail loans; 96% of transactions are digital.
Credit RWA to advances fell to 55.78% from 59.32%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there SMA or stress signals from West Asia, MSME or export clients?
qa_highlights.answer: SMA-to-credit ratio fell to 4.92% in March 2026 from 6.70% a year earlier. Management said no West Asia stress has shown in existing accounts so far, though individual cases may exist.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ECL provision buffer adequate?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,500 crore was added in Q3 and Rs 250 crore in Q4, giving Rs 1,750 crore. Total ECL impact is estimated at about Rs 3,000 crore, which will be front-loaded before April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said provisions were over-created by December quarter and actual requirements were lower, so staff expenses fell about Rs 200-250 crore in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect large treasury gains in the next two quarters given geopolitical uncertainty, and said the team will adjust its plan to market moves.

qa_highlights.question: How much growth could ECLGS 5.0 add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated Rs 8,000-10,000 crore of additional funding, with 25-30% of the portfolio eligible, subject to uptake.

qa_highlights.question: Liquidity and CD ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: No regulatory CD ratio limit exists. LCR was about 151% as of the day before the call, versus about 122-123% at March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Overseas NPAs and tax position?
qa_highlights.answer: Overseas NPAs are legacy 2015-2017 accounts in court; fresh slippage from overseas is negligible. No cash tax is payable given accumulated losses; FY26 tax demands of Rs 4,832-4,833 crore were offset by Rs 6,318 crore refunds over three years.

risks_watch: Credit growth at 24% may need more capital; CRAR is 19.78%, and ECLGS 5.0 uptake is still unproven.
Legacy overseas NPAs are about one-third of NPAs but are pending in court with no SARFAESI or DRT route; recoveries are needed to hold NNPA.
Agri exposure is about 35% of domestic advances; management flagged the monsoon forecast (94% of normal) as a risk outside Tamil Nadu crop loans.
Treasury gains are unlikely for two quarters; geopolitical uncertainty could affect NIM and bond portfolio.
Low free float; a QIP is planned for FY27 and government holds 92.44%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and consistent, with emphasis on continuity in growth, asset quality and capital. Management was more cautious on treasury gains and West Asia risk, and it gave direct answers on SMA, ECL and NIM.
key_quotes: So, SMA front is no challenge and that can be ascertained by the slippage ratios also.
And the idea is to front load the entire ECL requirement.
We are a commercial organization. We believe that growth is the lifeline.

adds.what: Domestic branches: about 160 added in FY26 (3,494 total, ~2,040 rural/semi-urban); no forward branch count given

growth.why: Management guides industry credit growth of 14-16% for FY27, which IOB expects to exceed while targeting 13-15% in key parameters, and NIM of 3.30-3.35%; backing is partial (retail/agri momentum, 24.16% advances growth, Rs 13,000 crore corporate pipeline, QIP plan) with no capacity-linked numbers beyond branch additions.
